definitions.explanation: A sound made by something, especially an unexpected or unidentified noise.

examples.japanese: {夜中|よなか}に{物音|ものおと}がして{目|め}が{覚|さ}めた。
examples.english: I woke up because of a noise in the middle of the night.

examples.japanese: {物音|ものおと}ひとつしない{静|しず}かな{夜|よる}だった。
examples.english: It was a quiet night without a single sound.

examples.japanese: {隣|となり}の{部屋|へや}から{物音|ものおと}が{聞|き}こえる。
examples.english: I can hear sounds from the next room.

notes:
{物音|ものおと} refers to an unidentified or unexpected sound — the kind of noise that catches your attention because you don't immediately know what caused it. Composed of {物|もの} (thing) + {音|おと} (sound).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {物音|ものおと}がする: a sound is heard (something makes a noise)
- {物音|ものおと}を{立|た}てる: to make a noise
- {物音|ものおと}ひとつしない: not a single sound (emphasizes complete silence)
- {物音|ものおと}に{気|き}づく: to notice a sound

USAGE:
Often used in stories and descriptions of quiet or tense situations — hearing a noise at night, silence in a room, etc. It has a slightly mysterious or uneasy nuance.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {音|おと}: sound (general, neutral — includes music, alarms, etc.)
- {騒音|そうおん}: noise (loud, disturbing, unwanted)
- {物音|ものおと}: noise (unidentified, draws attention)
